source.title: MarS: a Financial Market Simulation Engine Powered by Generative Foundation Model
source.authors: Junjie Li; Yang Liu; Wei-Qing Liu; Shi-Kai Fang; Le-Wen Wang; Chang Xu; Jiang Bian

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Evaluates scaling in a new setting—an autoregressive financial order-generation model—by varying model size and training tokens and reporting validation-loss curves.
record.gate_note: The paper reports validation-loss scaling curves and a downstream forecasting comparison. It does not report fitted power-law exponents, extrapolation from small runs, compute-optimal allocations, or a sweep over training compute. Cited scaling-law results from other work are not treated as findings here.
record.test_reason: The study trains two autoregressive transformer families on financial order data: an Order Model (2M–1.02B params) and an Order-Batch Model on VQGAN 'order images' (150M–3B). It reports validation loss against training tokens for each size (Fig. 3) and says loss improves with data and model size. This is a new-setting result bearing on V5, the scaling form beyond text. It also compares downstream forecasting accuracy for two model sizes (Fig. 7a). No power-law fit, exponent, extrapolation or compute-optimal analysis is reported.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors say LMM performance improves significantly with data and model size, consistent with scaling laws in other foundation models. They also say the 1.02B Order Model's lower validation loss goes with better forecasting than the 0.22B model.
record.recipe_differences: Uses financial order and order-batch autoregressive models and reports validation-loss curves over model size and training tokens; it does not reproduce the language-model scaling-law fitting or compute-optimal allocation procedures.
record.problems: Scaling and forecasting values are presented in plots rather than tables; no fitted power-law exponents, fit quality, or uncertainty for the scaling curves are reported. Only two Order Model sizes are compared for downstream forecasting.

untested.parts: Not a language model; no power-law fit of loss in parameters, tokens or compute.
No fixed-compute allocation or compute-optimal split.
Depth and width are not varied at fixed parameter count.
The power-law functional form and its exponents are not fitted. Only qualitative monotone improvement on a log-token axis is shown. Other modalities are not tested.
Predictability, i.e. a quantitative mapping from scale or loss to accuracy, is not established with only two sizes. Other tasks are not tested.
No comparison of fitting choices or curve bending.

record.verdict_notes: This is primarily a market-simulation systems paper; scaling is a brief section (2.1.3, Fig. 3) with no fits. Order Model training (32B tokens) exceeds the stated 16B-token dataset, so it involves data repetition. The Order-Batch loss is on VQGAN image tokens, which is relevant to V5's non-text framing. Both labels are weak: they are based on figure-only qualitative evidence.

versions.untested_parts: The systems are financial order-generation models, not language models; the paper does not test the stated language-model loss law.
No small-run fit is used to predict larger runs.
No fixed-compute allocation sweep or compute-optimal parameter/token split is reported.
Architecture details such as depth and width are not varied to test their effect at fixed parameter count.

Tests scaling with model size and training tokens for financial order-generation models; it does not establish fitted power-law forms or exponents, or test the other listed modalities and training regimes.

Tests the relation between model scale/pretraining validation loss and forecasting accuracy for two Order Model sizes; it does not test broader downstream tasks or establish a quantitative predictive mapping.
No comparison of fitting choices, exponents, setups, or curve bending is reported.

relationships.condition: Order Model (2M–1.02B) and Order-Batch image-token model (150M–3B) on Chinese stock order data
relationships.reason: Validation loss falls with more tokens and larger models across both families (r1–r13). Support is qualitative only: no power-law fit or exponent is reported.
relationships.display_finding: Validation loss decreased with more tokens and larger models in both model families, without a reported power-law fit or exponent.

relationships.condition: Order Model 1.02B vs 0.22B, trend-prediction accuracy at 1–5 min horizons
relationships.reason: The larger model, which has lower validation loss, outperforms the smaller one (r14–r18). Only direction is shown; two sizes cannot show predictability.
relationships.display_finding: The 1.02B model had lower validation loss and higher trend-prediction accuracy than the 0.22B model at every tested horizon.
